# dsh Container Image

**DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) as a batteries-included
container: agent, full toolchain, and reverse pro
xy in one image, built from the official source tags.**

Both examples publish `127.0.0.1:3081` and mount one volume at `/home/dsh`. The user layer
(`~/.dsh`

, caches, user-installed tools) survives image upgrades; the system layer comes from
the image. The

first visit is redirected to dsh's launch token, and the browser keeps the session
cookie from then
on, so there is no separate login form.
## What's inside
| Component | Description |

| Base image | `debian:13-slim` (moving tag; pass `BASE_IMAGE` to pin a digest) |
| Toolchain | Node
.js 24 LTS, pnpm, uv, Rust/cargo (+ rustfmt/clippy), git + git-lfs, build-essential + musl-tools, Ca

ddy, podman + crun, gh, yq. These are image-owned real binaries and upgrade with the image |
| Agent
CLI tools | ripgrep, fd, python3, zip, openssh-client, tmux, sqlite3, vim.tiny/nano, less, rsync, w
get, tree, htop, tzdata, patch, plus a diagnostics set (dig/nc/socat/traceroute/iperf3/nft, file, nc
du, strace, zstd/lz4, bc, moreutils, pv, uuid-runtime), xdg-user-dirs (UI default workspace) and dev
tooling (just, shellcheck). All of them are baked into the system layer, so a fresh container never

re-downloads them (a runtime `apt install` would be lost on recreation) |
| Nested containers | pod
man in-container (rootless) with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, subuid/subgid and the network/sysctl defaults pr
econfigured; the host runtime must allow unprivileged user namespaces + `/dev/fuse` + `/dev/net/tun`
and must not mask the container's `/proc` (`--security-opt unmask=ALL`, Quadlet `Unmask=ALL`, Docke
r `systempaths=unconfined`); resource limits (`--memory`/`--cpus`) inside nested containers are not

enforced (cgroup v2 constraint); see docs/deployment.md § In-container podman |
| dsh | Built from t
he official source tag into `/opt/deepseek-harness` (`DSH_TAG` pinnable; `latest` builds the newest

upstream tag, the only one the smoke gate verifies); no runtime auto-update |
| Exposure | Caddy rev
erse proxy (`0.0.0.0:3081` → dsh's `127.0.0.1:3080`); preserves the browser `Host`/`Origin`, redirec

ts the first visit to dsh's login token, and keeps optional basic auth |
| Supervisor | `dsh web` au

to-restarts on exit; `docker exec dsh dsh-restart` restarts it manually |

All container-side adaptation of upstream dsh (0.2.1-alpha.3 and newer) lives in **one Cordis plugin

**,

- **Launch-token redirect:** the plugin writes dsh's process launch token to
`/tmp/dsh-caddy/launch-

token`; Caddy 302s a browser without a session cookie to `/?token=...`, and
dsh sets an `HttpOnly; S

ameSite=Strict` cookie. The container never injects or rewrites the
session; the browser holds it.

patch.yml`; the legacy `settings.yaml` is imported once).

## Networking & security

- **Port model:** `dsh web` listens on `127.0.0.1:3080` (upstream rejects `--host 0.0.0.0`); the
exp

osed port is `3081`, published on host loopback by the examples.
- **The proxy preserves the fence:*

* Caddy forwards the browser `Host`/`Origin` unchanged, and dsh's
`/api` fence is real. External aut

horities must be listed in `DSH_TRUSTED_HOST` (or derived from
`DSH_PUBLIC_URL`); Caddy rejects any

other Host with 403, which is what stops DNS rebinding.
Anyone who can reach `3081` can log in, so e

nable basic auth (`DSH_PROXY_USER`/`DSH_PROXY_PASSWORD`,
set together or the supervisor refuses to s

tart) and keep the port firewalled. The
`/api/remote.mux` WebSocket is exempt from basic auth (brows

ers do not reliably attach
`Authorization` to upgrades) and is authenticated by the browser's `SameS

ite=Strict` cookie.
- **Session held by the browser:** the first visit without a cookie is 302'd to

dsh's launch token;
dsh sets the session cookie and the browser sends it back. There is no server-si

de cookie
injection. DeepSeek account sign-in still requires a loopback browser origin (an SSH tunne

l)
rather than a public hostname; see docs/deployment.md § DeepSeek account sign-in.
- **Streams, pa

yload and caching:** SSE/WebSocket pass through unbuffered (verified against Caddy
2.6) and dsh's 2

s heartbeat survives the hop. The client bundles are post-processed at build
time, so a cold page lo

ad measured in a headless browser is **≈1.6 MiB on the wire** against
≈5.8 MiB for upstream's unproc

essed payload. The combined client-plugin bundle drops from 5.06 MiB
to ≈1.0 MiB gzip, because image

s inlined at ≥ 100 KiB are extracted and fetched only when their
screen opens, and the bundles are m

inified. The index is `no-store` while the content-hashed
`/assets/*` tree is served `immutable`, so

repeat visits are cheap.
- **Telemetry off by default:** the entrypoint sets `DSH_TELEMETRY_MODE=DI

SABLED`, so the OTel
feedback uploader never sends anything unless you opt back in. Separately, upst

ream's
